feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: World leaders gathered for the annual BRICS summit. Here are the takeaways
entry.summary: India hosted the an annual summit which gathered leaders from 28 countries, including the presidents of China and Iran. Though, the U.S. was notably absent.

entry.title: Can Gulf states and Iran negotiate the Strait of Hormuz without the U.S.?
entry.summary: Dania Thafer of the Gulf International Forum weighs in on previously scheduled talks between Iran and Gulf states. Shortly before this interview aired, Oman announced that the talks were postponed.

entry.title: Indonesian passenger ship overturns, sparking search for at least 129 missing
entry.summary: Indonesian rescuers said about 130 passengers and crew are missing after a ferry carrying more than 240 people sank in bad weather in the Java Sea on Sunday.

entry.title: 'People are still afraid of those three letters': Fighting the stigma of HIV
entry.summary: That's a quote from former rugby star Gareth Thomas, who is HIV positive. At the International AIDS Conference in Rio this year, he spoke out about the isolation and discrimination tied to the virus.

entry.title: 'BRICS' forum brings together emerging economies, aimed at countering western dominance
entry.summary: India hosts the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi this weekend. BRICS is a grouping of major emerging markets and developing countries.

entry.title: Saudi Arabia forced to shut down crucial Red Sea pipeline after attacks
entry.summary: The Iran-backed Houthi militia captured a strategic Red Sea port city this week. NPR's Scott Simon talks to April Longley Alley of the Washington Institute.

entry.title: The secret quest to preserve Palestinian writer Raja Shehadeh's diaries
entry.summary: Leading Palestinian writer Raja Shehadeh has documented Israel's occupation of the West Bank since day one. Fearing the occupation might consume his archive, he secretly moved it to Scotland

entry.title: BRICS leaders meet in India as wars and US tensions test the bloc
entry.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosts Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and other leaders of the BRICS nations for a summit on trade, investment, and global conflicts.

entry.title: Yemen's Houthis capture a Red Sea island in threat to shipping
entry.summary: Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have captured a strategic island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The move threatens Saudi oil exports through a key commercial lane. And Saudi Arabia said it shut down a major oil pipeline as a precaution after it came under attack.

entry.title: The other side of 9/11: Afghans reckon with America's long shadow
entry.summary: It's been nearly 25 years since the start of the U.S- led invasion of Afghanistan. NPR returns to Kabul to see how Afghans, now back under Taliban rule, are coping with the legacy of that 20 year war.
